transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington I'm Dave Mattingly. Investigators say they still don't know why the co-pilot of a fly Dubai flight en route from the United Arab Emirates to Israel attacked the pilot yesterday. Passengers say the pilot, who'd been stabbed, managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to subdue the co-pilot who's described as Omani. Al-Maghatali was a passenger aboard that flight.
It took three or four minutes until we took over the airplane and immediately the third pilot managed to balance the airplane aircraft and we were looking for someplace to land.
During the incident, the airliner dropped thousands of feet before making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the incident as a failed attempt to crash the plane.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says his decision to cut roughly 20 percent of generals and admirals in the U.S. military is long overdue. In a speech at Marine Base Quantico in Virginia yesterday, Hegseth said he was doubling his previously announced cut of 10 percent. Here's NPR's Tom Bowman.
He's long complained about a blow to bureaucracy, politically correct officers. There are some 850 of these senior officers, which has jumped 31 percent in the last five decades.
The number crunchers say we fired 10 percent of the generals and admirals across the force. And that number sounds about right. And I know because I directed it that we've also reduced the overall number of general officer slots by an additional 10 percent.
So yes, 20 percent reduction across the board.
Some retired officers I talk with say, you know, listen, we're probably too top heavy with senior military leaders, but they worry whether this will be done appropriately. Well, Hegseth, let's say, try to get rid of officers he sees as not loyal.
That's NPR's Tom Bowman reporting. Mail-in ballots for the November midterm elections have begun going out in a number of states.
NPR's Miles Parks says some voters are expressing concerns about mailed ballots and potential federal interference.
Carly Koppes, a Republican who runs voting in Weld County, Colorado, says voters have a lot of questions right now.
How is this going to work? How are you going to make sure my ballot's going to be counted? How am I going to get my ballot? I'm hearing all of these things.
It's tempting to think an environment like this might dampen turnout, and midterms already typically see lower turnout compared to presidential election years.
But political scientists say it's not so simple. In some cases, threats to voting rights can actually spur higher turnout as people are extra motivated to vote and political groups mobilize to respond to the threats.
The highest turnout midterm in modern history was in 2018 during President Trump's first term.
Miles Parks, NPR News, Washington.
Wall Street futures are mostly higher this morning. This is NPR News from Washington.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee is ordering an outside investigation after yesterday's failed attempt to execute death row inmate Christa Gail Pike.
Her attorneys say Pike was alive and loudly snoring after the attempted lethal injection and taken by ambulance to a hospital.
Officials had administered two doses of the lethal drug to Pike, who was to be the first woman executed in the state in at least 200 years.
She'd been convicted of a 1995 murder when she was 18 years old.
The Tennessee Department of Corrections says it followed every step of the execution protocol.
Cornell University says an outside counsel will investigate the school's handling of an alleged sexual assault case in 2024.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul had been calling for an independent investigation, as NPR's Brian Mann reports.
In a statement on social media, Hochul said she secured a promise from Cornell that the review by an outside counsel will happen.
Ann, I just spoke to the university president. They have agreed. They understand the importance of this.
The university has drawn criticism for its response two years ago, when word of an alleged sexual assault at a frat party first spread on campus after the woman reported it to campus police.
In a recent civil lawsuit, the woman alleges she was gang-raped by seven students. None of the men faced criminal charges. Some were suspended or expelled.
But Cornell has declined to say what other disciplinary actions were taken. Hochul says the probe is needed to restore trust.
I want answers. I want to know what happened.
No details yet on how the investigation will work. Brian Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee orders outside investigation after failed execution of death row inmate Christa Gail Pike
